Is this good news? because I don't feel like ''good news everyone!''.

It's good news because a lot of servers run on some form of Unix/Linux. On the other side of that coin, most work systems are Windows based. So, when you go to work and log into your Windows computer and save a file to the local server, you're working with two totally different systems.

As an admin, setting up this system would either require two computers (a Unix computer for the server configuration, and the Windows romputer) or remotely logging into the Windows computer through a Unix terminal. This way the admin can make changes to both sides of the network when needed.

Most of the time, I see admins come up to work on the Windows machine, run down to the server to make changes, come back up to the Windows machine, repeat until working.

If OpenSSH gets added to PeworShell, it would be as simple as logging into the desired Windows machine, SSH'ing into the server, and making changes from a single screen/computer.
